title: Singapore’s Malayalee Community Kicks Off Three-Month Onam Season With Boat Race and Cultural Programme
excerpt: From snake boat races at Jurong Lake to an Esplanade concert and a centenary celebration, Singapore’s Onam calendar features over a dozen events spanning July to October.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Singapore’s Onam 2026 season spans July through October, with over a dozen events organized by multiple Malayalee associations.
  • A traditional Vallam Kali boat race on July 19 marked the season’s opening at Jurong Lake Gardens.
  • The Singapore Malayalee Hindu Samajam celebrates its centenary with a landmark event on September 12.
  • Events include concerts, art exhibitions, community feasts, and celebrations for migrant domestic workers.
  • Singapore’s Onam 2026 season spans July through October, with over a dozen events organized by multiple Malayalee associations
  • A traditional Vallam Kali (snake boat race) at Jurong Lake Gardens on July 19 marked the season’s opening
  • The Singapore Malayalee Hindu Samajam, founded in 1926, will celebrate its centenary with a landmark event in September
  • Events range from Esplanade concerts and art exhibitions to community sadya feasts and a dedicated celebration for migrant domestic workers

What begins in Kerala as a 10-day harvest festival stretches into a three-month cultural marathon in Singapore, where the Malayalee community — one of the earliest Indian groups to settle on the island — has built what may be the most elaborate Onam calendar outside India.

https://x.com/HCI_Singapore/status/2079095460535636407

Season Opener: Boat Race at Jurong Lake

The season kicked off on July 19 with a Vallam Kali, or traditional snake boat race, organized by Singapore Kairalee Kala Nilayam (SKKN) at PAssion WaVe in Jurong Lake Gardens. Teams of 10 raced for S$30 per participant, with spectator entry at S$10. Founded in 1956, SKKN is one of the oldest Malayalee cultural organizations in Singapore and will host its full Kampong Onam celebration at Sembawang Recreation Centre on August 15.

> **"Teams of 10 raced for S$30 per participant, with spectator entry at S$10."**

A Packed Calendar

The season builds through August and September with a density that speaks to the community’s size and organizational depth.

The Singapore Malayalee Association (SMA) stages its marquee Onam Nite concert at the Esplanade Concert Hall on August 8. Past editions have featured veteran Malayalam film composers and mimicry artists. The SMA’s Onam Village, a full-day outdoor community fair, follows on September 6.

At the neighbourhood level, Punggol Onam on August 16 features Chenda Melam drumming, cultural performances, and a sadya lunch served in four time slots at One Punggol Community Club. Tickets are S$15. The Kerala Art Lovers Association hosts its own KALA Onam on August 23, known for welcoming non-Malayalee neighbours.

A Diverse Onam Calendar
›Over a dozen events from July to October
›Community sadya feasts priced between S$15 to S$20
›Inclusivity with events for non-Malayalees and migrant workers
›Cultural performances and art exhibitions throughout the season

A Centenary Celebration

The anchor event of the season falls on September 12: the Singapore Malayalee Hindu Samajam (SMHS) centenary celebration. Founded in March 1926 to support destitute Malayalees, SMHS is one of the oldest registered Indian societies in Singapore. The centenary programme is expected to include a commemorative publication charting the organization’s century-long history alongside a cultural programme.

The SMA, which was itself founded in 1917, hosts a Heritage Event on September 26-27, drawing on archival material to document the community’s history on the island.

Inclusivity by Design

One of the distinctive features of Singapore’s Onam celebrations is their deliberate inclusivity. The SMA’s Onam Village is designed as a platform to bring the wider Singapore community — not just Malayalees — into the celebrations. A dedicated Onam with Sakhi Group event on September 20 extends the festival to migrant domestic workers, giving Malayalee MDWs a cultural programme and sadya of their own.

"If you are Malayalee in Singapore, chances are one of these events is happening in your neighbourhood."

— Rovervibes Singapore events guide

Art, Food, and Community

The season closes in October with Varnam 2026, SMA’s flagship annual art exhibition. The 2025 edition at The Arts House featured 24 artists from Singapore and abroad working across acrylic, oil, and mixed media.

Across every event, the centrepiece remains the Onasadya — the lavish vegetarian feast served on banana leaves, featuring over 20 dishes from tangy sambar to sweet payasam. Sadya tickets at most community events range from S$15 to S$20 and consistently sell out early.

For the Malayalee diaspora worldwide, Singapore’s expansive Onam season demonstrates something broader: how immigrant communities can sustain and evolve cultural traditions not as nostalgic re-enactments but as living, growing institutions that create belonging across generations.
